2610.06170.title: MS-Exam-Gen: Source-Grounded Benchmark Construction for Evaluating LLMs on Textual Multiple Sclerosis MRI Knowledge
2610.06170.paper_summary: Biomedical large language model (LLM) evaluation requires auditable assessment of narrow, evolving, source-grounded subspecialty knowledge. Multiple sclerosis MRI (MS-MRI) provides a high-stakes textual-knowledge test case because correct reasoning requires current diagnostic criteria, standardized acquisition and reporting knowledge, longitudinal monitoring concepts, lesion morphology, and recognition of difficult mimics. We present MS-Exam-Gen, a reproducible framework for constructing and auditing a text-based multiple-choice question (MCQ) benchmark for MS-MRI knowledge; it does not evaluate direct MRI image interpretation. MS-Exam-Gen targets source-grounded criteria, protocols, reporting, and differential diagnosis. The framework combines expert-source indexing, exam-oriented topic induction, evidence-grounded MCQ generation, automated quality audits, a same-family consistency screen, and empirical calibration. From a 66-source corpus indexed into 4,289 retrieval chunks, the pipeline produced a locked 3,058-item candidate benchmark spanning 16 topics and 53 subtopics. Evaluation across 12 primary LLM endpoints yielded 36,696 item-level predictions and separated performance over a 42.8-percentage-point accuracy range (89.7% to 46.9%). Across these endpoints, 25.5% of items were missed by at least four. Post-generation audits showed that refreshed construction reduced measurable answer cues, while option-order testing showed that absolute MCQ scores remain position-sensitive. Generated construction labels remain metadata rather than validated psychometric categories. Because expert adjudication and full option-order counterbalancing remain future work, MS-Exam-Gen is not a clinically certified examination. It should be interpreted as an automatically filtered, source-grounded candidate benchmark and reproducible audit workflow for item-level and topic-specific LLM evaluation.
2610.06170.paper_summary_zh: 生物醫學大型語言模型（LLM）的評估需要對狹窄、持續演變的來源基礎專科知識進行可審計的評估。多發性硬化症MRI（MS-MRI）提供了一個高風險的文本知識測試案例，因為正確的推理需要當前的診斷標準、標準化的獲取和報告知識、縱向監測概念、病變形態學以及對困難模仿的識別。我們提出了MS-Exam-Gen，一個可重複的框架，用於構建和審計基於文本的多選題（MCQ）基準，以評估MS-MRI知識；它不評估直接的MRI影像解釋。MS-Exam-Gen針對來源基礎的標準、協議、報告和鑑別診斷。該框架結合了專家來源索引、考試導向的主題引導、基於證據的MCQ生成、自動質量審核、同一家族一致性篩選和實證校準。從一個66個來源的語料庫中索引出4,289個檢索塊，該流程生成了一個鎖定的3,058項候選基準，涵蓋16個主題和53個子主題。在12個主要LLM端點的評估中，產生了36,696個項目級預測，並在42.8個百分點的準確率範圍內（89.7%到46.9%）分離了性能。在這些端點中，25.5%的項目至少被漏掉了四個。生成後的審核顯示，更新的構建減少了可測量的答案提示，而選項順序測試顯示絕對的MCQ分數仍然對位置敏感。生成的構建標籤仍然是元數據，而不是經過驗證的心理測量類別。由於專家裁定和完整的選項順序對照仍然是未來的工作，MS-Exam-Gen並不是一個臨床認證考試。它應被解釋為一個自動過濾的、來源基礎的候選基準和可重複的審計工作流程，用於項目級和主題特定的LLM評估。
